title: Bending stereocilia opens channels and starts an electrical signal
summary: When stereocilia on the hair cells bend, channels at their tips open and an electrical signal begins.
body: NIDCD says microscopic hair-like projections, stereocilia, perch on the hair cells. As the cells move, those projections bump an overlying structure and bend. Bending opens pore-like channels at the tips. Chemicals rush in and create an electrical signal. The page is describing that transduction step, not damage from loud noise.

sources.title: How Do We Hear?
sources.author: NIDCD
sources.note: Supports bending of stereocilia opening tip channels and creating an electrical signal.
